singleVersionStatus.reason: Three distinct exclusions, none of them drift. (1) Source 03 is excluded from re-acquisition by explicit decision and carries no export at any version; it remains a v2.1.2 artifact and any comparison including it is within-version only. (2) Sources 01, 02 and 04 sit at analyzer 2.6.0 while the eighteen sources added by the doctrine combo run (05-22) sit at 2.6.1, because the v2.6.1 patch was proven unable to move those three sources and re-running them was declined. (3) The pt10 tranche (23-30, added 2026-08-08) carries NO export at any version: it was archived to widen what the threshold sweep can see, and the sweep reads the .txt directly, so the eight sources entered the swept population without ever entering the export set. md/RERUN.md section 6 defines completion as every source carrying a current export at the epoch version, so by that literal test the corpus is not single-version and pt10 moved it further away rather than closer. What matters for the distillation lane is weaker and is still satisfied for the sources that have exports: all 21 analyzed sources share one analysis schema, one analyzer mode, one scoring configuration, and one canon snapshot (canonIndex.conceptCount 450 and provenance.identity.canonSnapshotHash 1v8z11a1xzrjgp are invariant across all 21 exports), so their claim surfaces are directly comparable. The pt10 eight are comparable to nothing yet, and analyzing them at today's v2.6.24 would put a THIRD analyzer version in the archive while the other 21 stay at 2.6.0/2.6.1 — which is a RERUN section 6 decision about the whole archive, not a step pt10 could take on its own.

chains.chain: archived raw HTML -> tools/extract-source-text.mjs -> the .txt whose SHA-256 is recorded here
chains.note: The extractor is committed (it is our code, not third-party text) so anyone holding the archived HTML can regenerate the exact analyzed text and check it against these hashes. Extraction was deliberately NOT done by a model reading the page: a model-mediated transcription is not reproducible byte-for-byte and would break the chain. Each source sidecar records its exact command line plus the SHA-256 of the raw capture it ran against.

chains.chain: archived raw PDF -> pdftotext 4.00 with recorded flags -> recorded awk anchor truncation -> the .txt whose SHA-256 is recorded here
chains.extractor: pdftotext (poppler / Glyph & Cog) version 4.00, external binary
chains.note: STRICTLY WEAKER THAN GRADE A and used only where the publisher ships no HTML full text. The chain is reproducible — same PDF bytes, same tool version, same recorded command, same output — but it depends on an external tool version rather than on a hashed file in this repository, so it cannot be verified from the repo alone. Each sidecar records the full command including the -nopgbrk flag (without it pdftotext injects page-break form feeds that defeat the line anchors) and the start/stop anchors used. No committed repo script reads PDFs; adding one was out of scope for this run.

chains.chain: archived raw discussion-API JSON (2 pages) -> a recorded body-concatenation one-liner -> tools/extract-source-text.mjs -> the .txt whose SHA-256 is recorded here
chains.extractor: tools/extract-source-text.mjs, preceded by the inline node command recorded in this source’s acquisition.method
chains.note: WEAKER THAN GRADE A in exactly one respect: the pre-step that flattens the API’s comment tree into HTML is recorded verbatim in the source entry rather than committed as a repo script, so a re-runner retypes it instead of hashing it. Everything else is the grade-A chain. The pre-step keeps comment BODIES only, in thread order with replies inline after their parent, and deliberately archives no usernames, timestamps or scores — the archive keeps what was said, not who said it.

reproducibility.scoutCaptureRule: Research scouts are model-mediated and their captures are therefore NEVER the archived artifact. Every source above was independently re-fetched and re-extracted by the orchestrator. Each entry records acquisition.scoutCrossCheck: 8-word shingle overlap between the scout capture and the deterministic extraction, which detects a scout that paraphrased, truncated, or invented prose. Overlap is corroboration of the scout, not provenance for the text.

labelingSheets.purpose: Peer-review artifacts with an empty VERDICT column, one per source. Section A grades every mapping (CORRECT/FALSE-POSITIVE), section B every unmapped claim-like passage (OK-NO-CANON/MISS), section C every passage the domain gate set aside (OK/SHOULD-HAVE-BEEN-RETAINED). A graded set becomes the fixture the threshold-calibration pass needs — today's thresholds were authored by judgment and never fitted to labelled data, which is what coverage.provisional records.
